analyzed_vuln.description: `unpack_hex` uses an `int count` parsed from the template and passes it directly to `mrb_str_new(mrb, NULL, count)` (line 838) without validating that `count` is non-negative / in-range. For the PoV format (`"h3333339010"`), `count` overflows/turns negative, so `mrb_str_new` receives a huge negative length. This reaches `str_new` -> `str_init_embed`, where `RSTR_EMBED_PTR(s)[len]` is indexed with that negative `len`, causing the UBSan out-of-bounds write in `mruby/src/string.c:74`. Root cause is missing bounds/overflow validation of unpack repeat count in `unpack_hex`/template handling before string allocation.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Via `mruby_fuzzer`, attacker-controlled Ruby source calls `String#unpack` with a crafted pack template containing a very large decimal repeat for hex unpack (`h...`). The parsed repeat count becomes invalid (negative via overflow), then `pack_unpack` dispatches to `unpack_hex`, which allocates a string using that invalid count. Trigger requires reaching `PACK_DIR_HEX` with overflowed count (as in PoV `s.unpack("h3333339010")`).
